item.text: {"classifications":[{"segment_id":"1","code":1,"rationale":"The President states an executive-branch policy objective, but this segment neither presently restricts transactions nor mandates a specified later legal result; implementation occurs elsewhere.","evidence":"It is the policy of the United States to restrict access by countries of concern"},{"segment_id":"2","code":2,"rationale":"The Attorney General must later issue regulations imposing specified prohibitions or restrictions on covered transactions; the legal consequences arise when those regulations take effect.","evidence":"shall issue, subject to public notice and comment, regulations that prohibit or otherwise restrict United States persons"},{"segment_id":"3","code":2,"rationale":"The Attorney General and Homeland Security Secretary must publish a proposed rule, security requirements, and guidance producing specified later regulatory constraints, notwithstanding accompanying implementation authority.","evidence":"shall, in coordination with the Attorney General and in consultation with the heads of relevant agencies, propose, seek public comment on, and publish security requirements"},{"segment_id":"4","code":4,"rationale":"This segment inseparably combines discretionary delegations and internal review directions, dictated requirements for later regulations, and present prohibitions on evasion and conspiracy.","evidence":"Any transaction or other activity that has the purpose of evading or avoiding, causes a violation of, or attempts to violate any of the prohibitions promulgated pursuant to this section is prohibited."},{"segment_id":"5","code":1,"rationale":"Officials must develop guidance and report on implementation, while the CFPB is only encouraged to consider action; these are internal guidance, reporting, and discretionary implementation measures.","evidence":"shall jointly submit a report to the President"},{"segment_id":"6","code":1,"rationale":"The specified officials must recommend possible risk-mitigation actions to the APNSA; the segment does not require adoption of any legal consequence.","evidence":"shall recommend to the APNSA appropriate actions to detect, assess, and mitigate national security risks"},{"segment_id":"7","code":1,"rationale":"The APNSA must internally review recommendations and may consult about implementation; no particular legal result is mandated.","evidence":"the APNSA shall review these recommendations"},{"segment_id":"8","code":1,"rationale":"The Attorney General must prepare an assessment report and solicit public comments, which are administrative study and reporting duties without a dictated legal outcome.","evidence":"shall submit a report to the President through the APNSA assessing, to the extent practicable"},{"segment_id":"9","code":1,"rationale":"Presidential advisers and agency officials must assess and recommend future regulation, while the definitions organize the order and largely leave operative thresholds and designations to later Attorney General regulations rather than themselves imposing the substantive restrictions.","evidence":"shall submit a report to the President, through the APNSA, assessing the risks and benefits of regulating transactions"}]}
